subtitles.en: Ship A: Book of the Watchers (1 Enoch 1-36) — 36 chapters. The Watchers myth + the throne-vision + Enoch's cosmic tours.

descriptions.en:
An English translation of 1 Enoch chapters 1-36 — the Book of the Watchers — produced from a per-verse layered witness reconstruction: Aramaic Dead Sea Scrolls fragments (4Q201/4Q202/4Q204/4Q205/4Q206/4Q207; the OLDEST surviving Enoch material, late 3rd c. BCE through 1st c. BCE) as the primary witness where preserved; Greek Akhmim Panopolitanus codex (6th c. CE; chs 1-32 substantially complete) as the secondary witness; Ge'ez (Ethiopic) as the tertiary witness and fallback for what neither Aramaic nor Greek preserves. The Ge'ez is the only complete witness to 1 Enoch but is the most-removed-in-time and -language from the original Aramaic composition.

The Raëlian canon (per Yes... I am Raelian commentary) names 1 Enoch among the texts 'closer to the truth' — alongside the Mahābhārata, Kojiki, Popol Vuh, and the Epic of Gilgamesh. The Watchers myth (chs 6-11) — the 200 fallen angelic 'Watchers' descending to take human wives + Asael (later Azazel) teaching humanity metallurgy, weapons-craft, cosmetics, magic, and astronomical-divination — is the canon's central interest. The text expands Genesis 6:1-4 (the bnei elohim + Nephilim notice) into a fully-developed mythological narrative.

Ship A scope: 36 chapters / Book of the Watchers. Ship B (chs 72-82 Astronomical Book) follows as a separate ship — the Aramaic DSS Astronomical Book (4Q208-4Q212; late 3rd c. BCE — the OLDEST Enoch fragments overall) is significantly longer than the Ge'ez recension, with much astronomical detail abbreviated in the Ge'ez transmission.

The text was canonical in the Ethiopian Orthodox Tewahedo Church (where it remains in the canon today) and the Beta Israel (Ethiopian Jewish) tradition. It is quoted explicitly in the New Testament (Jude 14-15 quotes 1 Enoch 1:9 + Jude 6 + 2 Peter 2:4 allude to the Watchers narrative) and was widely cited by 2nd-c. Church Fathers (Tertullian, Athenagoras, Justin Martyr) before falling out of Western and Eastern Orthodox + Roman Catholic canons in the 4th c. CE.

Cross-corpus density: extremely high. Cross-corpus to Genesis 6:1-4 bnei elohim; Jude 14-15 + Jude 6 + 2 Peter 2:4 (NT citations); Shi'ur Qomah + Hekhalot Rabbati throne-vision tradition; Ezekiel 1 + Daniel 7 + Revelation 4 throne-vision chain; the Watchers tradition in Jubilees + the Testament of Reuben + Origen + Augustine; the apkallū / Seven Sages Mesopotamian antediluvian-sages tradition (cross-corpus to Adapa + Gilgamesh XI L308).
